thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT — Private cluster 'acme-edge-03' (customer: ACME Corp) GPU queue length spiked to 580 (90th pct capacity). Autoscaler reported provisioning errors and did not add new nodes. Severity: P1. paging on-call now.

sara_oncall: I'm on it. seeing queue growth on the dashboard, logs show repeated node bootstrap timeouts (cloud-init failing at 90s). tagging infra. @mike_infra can you pick up?

mike_infra: oncall here, looking at the autoscaler stream. It kept hitting the limit: "scale_attempts_exceeded" and then "provision_timeout". There are 4 pending nodes in cloud provider for 12m. cloud provider returning 502 intermittently.

ryan_sre: quick customer impact note — ACME's prod routing to this private cluster. Telemetry: tail latency now 20s median, 95th ~120s, error rate 8% (gateway timeouts). Impacting about 18% of their token throughput.

jess_support: ACME support is seeing errors; they've opened a ticket and asked if we're throttling. I've informed them we have an incident and will share mitigation steps.

mike_infra: preliminary cause hypothesis: 1) node images failing to pull a large init artifact due to transient registry throttling, 2) autoscaler retries hit per-customer scale throttle (max_inflight_provisions). The autoscaler didn't fall back to less optimized instance types because a policy pinned instance type to 'p4d-large'.

sara_oncall: mitigation plan: 1) temporarily lift per-customer provision limit (if safe), 2) manually trigger a smaller instance type pool (p4d -> p3/ga100 variant) for this cluster, 3) route non-critical traffic to hosted fallback model. Trying 3 now.

ops-bot: routing rule applied: route 25% of customer 'acme' low-priority inference to hosted-fallback (model: rdx-small) — effective immediately.

mike_infra: starting manual provision of 2 smaller nodes to drain queue. Command I ran:
```
# trigger manual instance create (internal tooling)
redwood infra provision --cluster acme-edge-03 --type p3-xlarge --count 2 --reason "incident temporary scaleout"
```

mike_infra: logs from cloud API show repeated 502s and then a successful create for one node at +3m. The second node is stuck "provisioning".

sara_oncall: ops-bot, can you temporarily disable the strict instance-type pin for this cluster? We'll allow fallback pool for 10m.

ops-bot: policy update applied: instance-type-pin disabled for acme-edge-03 for 10 minutes (audit id: audit-1977723344-01).

ryan_sre: good — autoscaler has now enqueued two p3 nodes and one succeeded. Queue depth declining from 580 -> 220 in ~5m. Latency dropping to median 6s. Keep monitoring.

mike_infra: still seeing some node bootstrap logs failing due to `cloud-init: error fetching artifact` — attaching snippet:
```
ERROR cloud-init[45]: failed to fetch https://reg-private/agent-init.tar.gz: 502 Bad Gateway
TRACE infra: retrying download (attempt 3/5)
```
We asked cloud provider / registry team to escalate.

sara_oncall: customer comms: jess, please tell ACME we have partial mitigation (some traffic routed to fallback; nodes being added) and we're seeing recovery but there may be residual delays for ~15-30m.

jess_support: sending note now.

mike_infra: follow-up mitigation: enabling temporary KV-cache bypass so requests don't queue behind warmup batches for a short period. Command: `redwood runtime update-config --cluster acme-edge-03 --kv-bypass true --ttl 300s`

ryan_sre: note — enabling kv-bypass increases per-token CPU/GPU cost, but reduces queuing. Approving.

sara_oncall: handoff plan: I'm going offline at +20m. @mike_infra you'll be primary, @ryan_sre shadow. If anything regresses (queue >400 or error rate >10%) page the oncall again.

mike_infra: ack. I'll keep the incident channel updated. Current metrics: queue 190, error rate 3.5%, median latency 5.8s.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: TEMPORARY MITIGATIONS APPLIED — routing fallback (25%), manual smaller nodes provisioning, instance-pin disabled for 10m, kv-cache bypass enabled. Incident timeline ID: 1977723344.

sara_oncall: posting incident summary to the incidents tracker now. I'll add root cause hypothesis and next steps (audit registry throttles, review per-customer provision caps, consider autoscaler backoff tuning, add fallback auto-policy when pinned types fail).

jess_support: ACME acknowledged a follow-up call in 1h.

mike_infra: once registry stabilizes, recommend draining p3 nodes and reintroducing pinned p4 capacity with a staged rollout.

ryan_sre: adding one actionable: create an autoscaler policy that if provisioning attempts fail >3x in 5m, automatically enable fallback instance pool and reduce per-customer concurrency for new requests — to prevent large queue spikes.

sara_oncall: agreed. adding to post-incident RFC. Thanks everyone. closing active paging in 10m if stable. :wave:

mike_infra: closing note at 1977723660: cluster stabilized, queue <50, error rate <1%. Will monitor for 2h and follow up with detailed RCA.
